module_title: Intermediate Protocols and Port Numbers (IMAP, UDP, Telnet)
introduction: This intermediate tier introduces alternative protocols (IMAP, UDP) and the highly tested concept of 'Port Numbers'. Every protocol uses a specific digital 'door' (port) to enter and exit a server, and memorizing these is crucial for banking and SSC exams.

core_concepts.title: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)
core_concepts.description:
An advanced alternative to POP3 for 'Receiving' emails. 
Difference: POP3 downloads the email and deletes it from the server (single device). IMAP leaves the email on the server and merely 'Syncs' it, allowing you to view the exact same inbox across your phone, laptop, and tablet simultaneously.

core_concepts.title: UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
core_concepts.description:
The alternative to TCP. It is 'Connectionless'. It sends data incredibly fast but does NOT check if the data actually arrived (no guarantee of delivery). 
Usage: Used in Live Video Streaming, Online Gaming, and VoIP calls where speed is more important than perfect accuracy.

core_concepts.title: Telnet (Teletype Network)
core_concepts.description: A protocol used for 'Remote Login'. It allows a user to connect to a remote computer over the internet and control it using a command-line interface, as if they were sitting right in front of it.

core_concepts.title: What are Port Numbers?
core_concepts.description: While an IP Address gets data to the correct computer, a 'Port Number' gets data to the correct Application inside that computer. (Analogy: IP Address is the building number; Port Number is the specific apartment number).

important_entities.name: Crucial Port Numbers List
important_entities.significance:
- HTTP = Port 80
- HTTPS = Port 443
- FTP = Port 20 and 21
- SMTP = Port 25
- POP3 = Port 110

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a statement-based question asks 'Which protocol allows you to sync emails across multiple devices?', never choose POP3. POP3 is traditionally single-device only. The correct answer is always IMAP.
Examiners will test reliability. TCP is 'Reliable' because it takes acknowledgments. UDP is strictly 'Unreliable' because it fires data without waiting for receipts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 25 to Send, 110 to Drop, 143 to Sync
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: SMTP (Send) is the lowest port: 25. POP3 (Download/Drop) is 110. IMAP (Sync) is 143.

exam_strategy_tips: In IT Officer and SSC CGL exams, HTTP Port 80 and HTTPS Port 443 are the most frequently asked port numbers. Lock them into your memory.
